local_dishes.name: Baursak
local_dishes.description: Soft fried dough bites, often served with tea or honey; a popular snack and staple of festive meals.

local_dishes.name: Kuurdak (veg version)
local_dishes.description: Can be made with potatoes and onions.

local_dishes.name: Plov (veg)
local_dishes.description: Rice pilaf with carrots and sometimes chickpeas; ask for no meat (bez myasa).

local_dishes.name: Lagman (veg)
local_dishes.description: Hand-pulled noodles in a broth with vegetables; request without meat.

local_dishes.name: Manti (veg)
local_dishes.description: Dumplings, usually with meat; Korean or Uyghur places offer veg versions (pumpkin, potato).

local_dishes.name: Beshbarmak (veg)
local_dishes.description: Rare, but some restaurants serve vegetarian versions with noodles and mushrooms.

local_dishes.name: Beshbarmak
local_dishes.description: Kazakhstan's national dish of boiled meat served over flat noodles and broth; the name means 'five fingers' as it was historically eaten by hand.
local_dishes._source_file: Almaty Kazakhstan/Uzbekistan and Kazhakstan- All Inclusive Guide_13032026.docx

local_dishes.name: Manty
local_dishes.description: Kazakhstan's version of steamed dumplings, often larger and typically filled with minced meat and onions.

Kazakh tea sets and ceramics: colorful porcelain bowls (piala) and teapots with national patterns or eagle motifs
Local spices and dried goods: wild herbs, dried apricots, nuts, saffron and kurt (fermented cheese balls)
Embroidery and traditional clothing: embroidered jackets, slippers, skullcaps (takiya) and robes
Books, folk art and mini yurts: hand-painted folk wooden art and portable felt yurts
